mx.teacher_note: The cell membrane gives plant cells rigidity and strength.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Chloroplasts can carry out photosynthesis even without chlorophyll.

mx.teacher_note: Photosynthesis produces the chlorophyll in chloroplasts.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Every plastid in every plant part carries out photosynthesis.

intelligence.enrichment: In plant cells, the cell wall provides rigidity and strength. Plant cells have plastids, and chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which makes them green and helps in photosynthesis. Fungal cells have a cell wall but do not have chloroplasts. Cell wall -> rigidity and strength; chloroplasts with chlorophyll -> green colour and photosynthesis; absence of chloroplasts in fungi -> no chloroplast-based photosynthesis. The learner correctly applies this rule: In plant cells, the cell wall provides rigidity and strength. Plant cells have plastids, and chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which makes them green and helps in photosynthesis. Fungal cells have a cell wall but do not have chloroplasts. The cell membrane is the outside covering, so it must explain firmness, green colour, and photosynthesis.
